Stacks recently released its Q3 report with updates.

Here's a short TL;DR + some of my thoughts ↓

→ Bitcoin Staking

The first two staking rounds brought in 735 BTC, with 21Shares, HashKey Cloud, and UTXO Management among the participants.

→ Liquid Staking

@StackingDao accounted for 483 BTC of the 505 BTC in the second round. It now has 636 BTC worth of stBTC in circulation.

→ STX Staking

The amount of STX staked has grown by over 25% since the PoX-5 upgrade, from 392M to 493M STX.

→ Lending

@ZestProtocol now has over $122M in deposits and $42M in loans, with around 800 BTC used as collateral.

→ Trading

Trading across Stacks DEXs reached $16.7M in a single week in September, the highest in a year, with @Bitflow leading the activity.

My guess is that BTC staking will end up benefiting more than just the staking protocols.

More people borrowing against their staked BTC → more activity in lending markets and DEXs → more fees going to different parts of the ecosystem.

Quite the opportunity for the entire ecosystem.

Disclosure: I'm a long-time $STX holder and Stacks supporter.

if an ai you like talking to holds it’s worldview in it’s weights/associations/dataFrame then kinda by definition there’s going to be a statistical relationship between the shape of that data and the outside world 

the question of can we tie neurons to concepts, in a one for one manner(!), is more a question about what researchers are capable of vs the content of the tree/map

meaning wouldn’t it be nice for us hoomans if we could find a single neuron that tied enough to a concept or behavior we could use it to drive or tune an LLM like a car

and yes it would be nice, and maybe we can find a way to train models to constraint them in that way someday, but seems far more likely the behavior-button will be some weighting of neurons that already exist 

“Golden Gate Claude” etc 

and then our alignment work becomes building and driving these nets of behavior on top of nets of knowledge or whatever 

with different kinds of model architectures and training structures 

which sounds like a beautiful mess

anyway, that’s the crux imho 

race between alignment and capabilities 

which is why yud is being such a bear re mech interp, cognitive dissonance etc etc

🔶 COPPER
Trading around $6.50/lb, still roughly 32% above a year ago. This week also highlighted a crucial distinction: copper stockpiled in the U.S. does not automatically solve supply needs elsewhere. Watch inventory location alongside headline totals.

🥇 GOLD
Around $4,165/oz late Friday, down approximately 0.7% for the week. Hotter inflation revived rate-hike concerns, leaving gold caught between inflation protection and the pressure from higher interest rates.

My view heading into the weekend: stay selective. Prioritize projects that can turn resources into production—and companies with the funding to get there.

The next leg needs execution. ⚒️

By January 2020, David sought to end the relationship, but Knouse apparently did not want it to end.  When David thereafter started a new relationship and Knouse learned about it, she began a secretive campaign to destroy him by attempting to end his career as a scientist.  She did so by damaging his name, reputation, and that of his family with false sexual harassment and other claims, thereby making him unemployable.

Knouse conspired with Dr. Ruth Lehmann, the then- and still current Director (i.e., President) of the Whitehead Institute, in her efforts to destroy Sabatini.  

The record presented in court demonstrated that Dr. Lehmann committed to Knouse in October of 2020 that she would fire David. Dr. Lehmann made this commitment to Knouse before any investigation of the facts had taken place. 

Seven months after committing to fire him, in March of 2021, Dr. Lehmann, on behalf of the Whitehead, hired the law firm of Hinckley, Allen, Snyder (HAS) to undergo an investigation of David.  By July 2021, HAS shared a draft of its conclusions with MIT, HHMI, and the Whitehead, but not with David or his lawyers. 

On the morning of August 19, 2021, David for the first time received the more than 200-page investigative report and a calendar invite for a meeting the following day with Dr. Lehmann, the president of HHMI, and the HR directors of both institutions. The report was riddled with errors and unsupported claims about David and his relationship with Knouse.

When David's lawyer immediately thereafter reached out to Whitehead counsel to ask whether David was about to be fired, they confirmed that he would be terminated at the meeting.

An attractive target with David, one of the most important scientists of his generation in line for the Nobel Prize, a purported inappropriate sexual relationship with a younger female colleague, and a political and institutional environment where punishing a man for sexual harassment advanced the career and reputation of the person and/or institution that destroyed the career and reputation of the accused, regardless of the validity of the allegations.

As a result of Knouse's claims, Lehmann's sham investigation, and the media onslaught that followed, David lost all sources of income and his reputation was destroyed.  All prizes he had been previously been awarded were withdrawn.  He was removed from all scientific advisory and other honorary roles other than as a member of our family foundation's (the Pershing Square Foundation's) scientific advisory board.

Today, a 13-person jury (seven men and six women) of David Sabatini's peers (12 jurors plus an alternate) unanimously determined that David proved that Kristin Knouse defamed him, tortiously interfered with his contractual relationships (his entire career as a scientist), and tortiously interfered with his prospective advantageous relationships (his future employment). The jury rejected all of Knouse's claims including her claims that David engaged in quid pro quo sexual harassment and created a sexually hostile work environment.

Dr. Lehmann nearly killed David with her actions, as had we not rescued David by finding him employment, supporting him publicly to buffer the reputational damage, and supporting his recovery, he could have ended his life and left his son without a father before the world understood what had transpired here.

And the reputational damage was not just to David.  

David's brother, Bernardo Sabatini, is one of the most important neuroscientists in the world.  To this day, he has had to deal with a large cloud over his family name and reputation.  Recently, when the new CEO of our brain institute mentioned that Bernardo Sabatini was on our board, he was asked: "Wasn't he involved in some kind of sex scandal?"

We have unfortunately seen massive amounts of scientific fraud which has harmed innumerable human lives and wasted billions of dollars of research funding and time.

For her ethical breaches here, Dr. Lehmann should be fired from the Whitehead.  Based on her actions in this case, she is in no position to serve as the leader of an important scientific institute.  

I speak with some perspective on how scientific and other institutions should be led.  Including the recent launch of the Ackman Oxman Institute, we have funded approximately $1 billion of scientific research and institutions over the last decade or so, and this experience has given us the opportunity to meet the leadership of many of the most important scientific institutions in the world.  

To put it plainly,  we would not give a dollar to a scientific institute whose leader compromised basic moral principles as has happened here.

At an absolute minimum, the board of the Whitehead should immediately launch a detailed and independent investigation of Dr. Lehmann's actions in the Sabatini case.  I would encourage the investigation, among other considerations, to carefully exam all of the correspondence between Lehmann and Knouse, as well their correspondence with the HAS law firm on among other areas, the various drafts of the Sabatini investigative report.

Alternatively, Dr. Lehmann could resign, minimize further distraction for the Whitehead, and save institutional time and resources that would be better spent on research that benefits humanity.

I went from working with one agent in a chat to sitting in tmux monitoring 6 agents in parallel in my terminal.

And honestly that's about the limit of my brain. I'm constantly switching between them, remembering what each one is doing, checking who's stuck and who needs me. It's exhausting!

I can’t do that with 100 agents. Or 200. Definitely not a swarm of 200k.

The more I work this way, the more obvious it becomes that it's the wrong form factor. Even with a nice UI, I'm not going to click through every agent to figure out what's going on.

What I need is a feed. A command center that tells me what happened, what's stuck, what needs a decision from me and what I should look at next. So let the agents coordinate the work. Bring me in when I can actually help.

I want to run more agents without spending the rest of my life watching them.
